reviews.body: Tubed the full run on a Tuesday and it was close to empty. Water is genuinely cold, about 72, so give yourself a minute before pushing off. The tram back was running every 20 minutes.
Beautiful, but the north entrance had already closed to new cars by 10 on a Saturday. Went to the south entrance instead and got in with no wait.
Clearest water I have swum in. Bring water shoes for the limestone and do not underestimate how far the tube run is with small children.
Lovely spring, but we queued 40 minutes at the gate and the lot filled before we reached the front. Go early or go midweek.
The headspring basin is enormous and the gardens are worth the walk on their own. Reservation for the head springs entrance was quick to book the night before.
Swim area is roped and shallow at the edge, good for children. Concession tube rental ran out by midday.
Busy but well managed. Plenty of shade near the picnic area, which matters in August.
Went in September so swimming was open. In winter the manatees take over and the water closes, so check before you drive.
Boardwalk along the run is the best part. Parking filled by 10:30 and they were turning cars away at the gate.
Swam the run from the boil down to the dock. Cold, clear and deep in the middle.
Easy drive from Orlando which is exactly why it fills early. Swim area is concrete edged and shallow, more of a pool than a wild spring.
Arrived at 11 on a Sunday and the park was already at capacity. Came back at 3 and got straight in.
Rented a canoe and paddled up the run. Saw two otters. Worth doing before you swim.
Private park so the rules are different: alcohol is allowed and it gets loud on summer weekends. Water is spectacular and the diving is the real draw.
Went on a holiday weekend and it was closer to a festival than a spring. Beautiful water, but not what we wanted with young children.
Midweek in the shoulder season it is close to perfect. Camped overnight and had the Devil's Eye area almost to ourselves at dawn.
The pancake house is the reason half the queue exists. Spring itself is a walled basin, very easy to get in and out of.
Swim area was open and clear. Put your name down for a griddle table before you swim, the wait runs over an hour.
Boardwalk out to the Suwannee is lovely and the spring run is shallow enough to wade. Vultures everywhere, which is stranger than it sounds.
River was high after rain so the spring was tea coloured. Staff were upfront about it at the gate.
Floating the run at Rock Springs is the best hour you can have for a few dollars. Get a reservation, they sell out days ahead in summer.
Arrived without a reservation on a Thursday and still got in at 9:15. By 10 the lot was full.
Small, quiet and gorgeous. Capacity is genuinely limited so they close the gate early on weekends.
One of the newer state parks and it shows, facilities are tidy. Short walk from the lot to the water.
Pleasant stop rather than a destination. The spring is small and the river was murky when we went.
Steep steps down to the spring and no lifeguard. The sunken steamboat is visible from the bank when the water is clear.
Natural limestone bridge over the spring is unusual and worth seeing. Very quiet midweek.
Was closed for swimming when we visited. The boardwalk and picnic area were still open and pleasant.
Buccaneer Bay is a water park attached to a spring, so expect slides and crowds rather than wilderness. Children loved it.
Reached capacity before 10 on a Saturday and they close the whole park, not just the water. The mermaid show is genuinely charming.
